title: Write session tokens into the access report as text

blocks.text: The access report is a CSV file built from rows whose cells come from several services, so `CsvExport` receives each row as a `List<?>`. The auth service keeps session tokens as `char[]`, so it can wipe them after use. Support has noticed that the token column of last night's report reads `[C@5e91993f`, `[C@1c4af82c` and so on, and that rows from the batch import show `null` where a cell was simply empty.

Finish `cell(Object value)` in `src/main/java/practice/CsvExport.java`. A token cell is written as the characters it holds, an empty cell (`null`) as nothing at all, and every other cell as `String.valueOf` writes it. `line(...)` already joins the cells with commas. About three lines in total.

cases.says: strings, numbers, booleans and characters are written as their usual text, joined with commas
a char[] cell is written as its characters, although the cell reaches the code typed as Object
a null cell is written as an empty field, not as the text null

origin.section: The Interface's Parameter Types Choose the Overload; the Value at Run Time Doesn't

concepts: The chosen overload decides what a null does: valueOf(Object) writes "null", valueOf(char[]) throws.

The functional interface's parameter types choose which overload a reference names, once, at compile time; the argument's run-time class plays no part, so String::valueOf as a Function<Object, String> writes [C@... for a char[].
